# shad0w

> shad0w (pip install shad0wllm, npm i shad0wllm) learns the fixed-choice decisions an application sends to an LLM
> (intents, routing, moderation, agent tool choice), and answers the ones it can certify from a small table on the CPU in
> microseconds. Every other request still goes to the LLM, and its answer is logged so the table keeps learning. The
> certificate (Learn-then-Test with Clopper-Pearson bounds) states that, among served answers, disagreement with the LLM
> is at most alpha (default 5%) with 90% confidence. It works in front of chat models, the OpenAI Decisions API and System
> One decision models (Jev, Kev, Laya), from Python, JavaScript, C or HTTP, or with zero code through an OpenAI-compatible
> proxy. Apache-2.0, by Gaurav Chauhan.

## Blog
- [shad0w at work: five jobs real teams can give it](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/five-jobs.html): Support routing, a prompt guard, product photos, a live data stream and a zero-code proxy: what shad0w does in each, the code, and what it measured.
- [shad0w 0.4: one reflex for text, images and guards](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/one-reflex-every-input.html): shad0w 0.4 takes its learned table and certificate from text to pixels, prompt-injection guards and video frames. What works, what doesn't, and what to try.
- [Zero-code System Zero for the OpenAI Decisions API](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/decisions-api-proxy.html): Point the OpenAI Decisions API client at the shad0w proxy: certified questions come back from a table in microseconds, the rest go upstream. No code change.
- [Snake at 120 moves a second: System 0 vs System One](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/game-speed.html): shad0w, three System One decision models and a hosted LLM play the same snake games at game speed. shad0w keeps scoring; the LLM falls behind its own moves.
- [94.3%, 51.3%, 0%: honest numbers against a hosted LLM](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/honest-numbers.html): What shad0w answered, and missed, when it shadowed a hosted LLM through the official OpenAI client: wins, losses and the traffic where it should defer.
- [Adding a category without breaking production](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/adding-a-category.html): A trained shortcut and a changing list of options are a dangerous mix. The rule shad0w follows, and what happens when you add, remove or rename an option.
- [System Zero: the reflex layer below your LLM](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/system-zero.html): Below your LLM (System 2) and decision models (System 1) there is room for a reflex: System 0, a table that answers repeat decisions in microseconds.
- [How shad0w proves it agrees with your LLM](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/blog/how-the-certificate-works.html): The certificate behind shad0w, in plain words: a held-out test, a confidence line, an allowance for bad luck, and what the promise does and does not cover.

## Watch and play
- [shad0w at work (film, 2 min)](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/#film): what it is, then five jobs: support routing, a prompt guard, product-photo sorting, live-stream labelling, a zero-code proxy; and how you start. MP4 at https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/assets/shad0w-film.mp4
- [Snake arena](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/arena/): shad0w, small decision models and a hosted LLM play the same snake games at game speed
- [Can System 0 run Doom?](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/doom/): an LLM plays ViZDoom with the game paused; shad0w learns its choices and plays every tic in microseconds, against the LLM in real time (recorded, replayed)
- [Decision Bench](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/bench/): shad0w against five open decision models on six public tasks, CPU only, same rows and same 5% certifier; every prediction saved
- [Playground](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/playground/): every live demo and game in one place
- [Doodle Duel](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/doodle/): a drawing game; a shad0w image table (no neural network) guesses your doodle on every stroke in microseconds
- [Prompt guard](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/guard/): block known prompt-injection attacks in microseconds in the browser, block-only (never allows on the table's word)
- [One minute of Polymarket, labelled live](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/pulse/): press start and the browser reads every Polymarket trade for 60 seconds; a shad0w table built from Polymarket's own tags files each by section and topic in microseconds, checked live against those tags, with a downloadable CSV
- [Duel: a 1v1 rifle fight against shad0w](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/duel/): a first-person browser game whose opponent's tactics were learned from an LLM and decided 60 times a second
- [Play Pong against shad0w](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/pong/) · [Playground: a 77-intent table in your browser](https://2796gaurav.github.io/shad0w/demo/)
